definitions.explanation: A developed or systematic way of thinking about something.
A system of ideas and ideals, especially concerning political or social matters.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{思想|しそう}は{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}に{影響|えいきょう}を{与|あた}えた。
{自由|じゆう}と{平等|びょうどう}は{民主主義|みんしゅしゅぎ}の{基本的|きほんてき}な{思想|しそう}だ。
examples.english: Freedom and equality are fundamental ideas of democracy.

examples.japanese: {東洋|とうよう}{思想|しそう}と{西洋|せいよう}{思想|しそう}には{大|おお}きな{違|ちが}いがある。それぞれの{文化|ぶんか}や{歴史|れきし}が{反映|はんえい}されている。
examples.english: There are major differences between Eastern and Western thought. Each reflects its own culture and history.

notes:
{思想|しそう} refers to systematic thought, ideology, or philosophical ideas, often in intellectual, political, or social contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {政治|せいじ}{思想|しそう} (political ideology)
- {宗教|しゅうきょう}{思想|しそう} (religious thought)
- {哲学|てつがく}{思想|しそう} (philosophical thought)
- {思想|しそう}の{自由|じゆう} (freedom of thought)
- {思想|しそう}{家|か} (thinker, philosopher)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {思想|しそう}: systematic thought/ideology (more abstract, philosophical)
- {考|かんが}え: thought, idea (everyday thinking)
- {意見|いけん}: opinion (personal view on a matter)
